name: 梅利纳·埃斯
introduction: Melina Hess is a Swiss-French film and television professional whose multifaceted career spans production, directing, and performance. She began her journey in the arts as an actress at the age of six, before expanding into film production and festival work.With over a decade of experience across the European film industry, Hess has established herself as a versatile force on set. Her work includes key production roles on major projects such as The Palace (dir. Roman Polanski), the Netflix series Die Beschatter II, and The Bends (dir. Mike Barker, for Disney+), where she served as personal assistant to the director. She was also part of the award-winning Navalny documentary during the covid-19 pandemic, showcasing her ability to manage complex productions under extraordinary circumstances.In addition to her production experience, Melina is a skilled interpreter and live host, working fluently in French, German, and English. She has served for several years as live interviewer at the Munich Film Festival, conducting Q&As with international talent including Isabelle Huppert and Jean-Jacques Annaud.Melina is passionate about creating safe, inclusive environments on set, having frequently taken on informal mediator roles during multilingual productions. In 2025, she applied for a certification program to become an official Vertrauensperson (confidant) in film and culture, reflecting her commitment to ethical and respectful collaboration in the industry.Outside of her professional commitments, Hess continues to nurture personal creative projects, including the independent comedy Home Swiss Home, shot during the covid-19 pandemic, in which she acted and contributed behind the scenes. The film premiered at the OtherMovie Film Festival in Lugano.She holds degrees in Acting and Film Production from the Universität der Künste Berlin, and is certified in advanced English at a C2 level by IELTS. Her trilingual fluency and rich experience across departments make her a rare and dynamic presence in European cinema.
